## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `successor-representation-map`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-08T23:04:09.486Z.

Planning pass 2026-07-09 (fifth follow-up): Algorithm (16) successor-representation predictive map over agent trajectories (serves pm-vvib candidate 17 cognitive map). Purpose: give agents ORIENTATION — region, landmarks, goal direction, latent shortcuts — as folded derived state, the computational account of hippocampal cognitive maps (Dayan's successor representation; Stachenfeld et al.: place cells encode expected discounted future state occupancy, grid cells are the SR's eigenvectors). Mechanism, three stages. Stage 1 — trajectory extraction: each agent's episodic stream already records the ordered sequence of items it touches (mutations, plus retrieval events from algorithm 14 stage 1); fold same-author time-windowed transitions i→j at write time (algorithm 6), O(1) per mutation, replayable from the immutable streams. Stage 2 — SR maintenance: maintain M(i,j) ≈ expected discounted future occupancy of j given presence at i via incremental TD(λ)-style updates per folded transition; at scale, never hold the full matrix — keep a top-d spectral embedding (the "grid-cell" basis) with sketch-backed state (algorithm 8), so storage is O(items × d) and updates stay local; ACT-R log-time decay (algorithm 1) ages transitions so decade-old traffic patterns fade without cliffs. Stage 3 — map services, all read-time and bounded: (a) ORIENTATION — regions emerge as clusters in SR-embedding space (traversal-defined, complementing declared-hierarchy chunking in algorithm 9); landmarks = highest stationary-occupancy hubs (milestone/epics/ADRs surface naturally); the pm context orientation block renders focus item's region, nearest landmarks with hop counts, and expected-steps-to-goal. (b) GOAL-CONDITIONED DISTANCE — expected traversal steps between focus and the agent's claimed milestone read directly off the SR, a principled next-step input to pm next's ranking (which item moves me toward my goal, not just which is globally ready). (c) SHORTCUT INFERENCE — high SR similarity between items/regions with NO declared edge and NO co-change support = a latent route worth surfacing as an advisory edge (pm-4ri6 surface); complements algorithm 12 co-change (pairwise same-burst coupling) because SR composes MULTI-STEP discounted paths — it predicts where work LEADS, not just what it touches together. (d) ZOOM — coarse SR eigenvectors give large-scale regions, finer ones give local structure, exactly the multi-scale levels candidate 17 serves; packing (algorithms 4/9) prices each zoom level like any representation level. Explainability (3): every orientation line decodes to its occupancy statistics ("region: release-tooling — you touched 7 of its items this week; landmark pm-doxj, 2 hops; goal ~4 steps via pm-wrbe"). Distinct from (2) spreading activation (one-shot cue diffusion at read time over explicit edges; SR is a LEARNED long-horizon expectation folded at write time), from (12) co-change mining (pairwise burst statistics; SR is sequential, discounted, and composes routes), and from (10) WL fingerprints (static structural shape; SR is dynamic traversal statistics — two identically-shaped subgraphs can occupy opposite ends of the traffic map). Spectrum behavior: small/young workspaces — transitions are too sparse for regions to form, SR stays near-diagonal, orientation block suppressed below threshold, cost one fold per mutation; million-item thousand-agent workspaces — the map is the only sublinear way for a cold agent to orient and route without scans, and per-agent trajectories fold independently so concurrency needs no coordination beyond the existing append-only streams.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
